questions.questionText: 132 engineers are to be allocated to two projects in the ratio 4 : 7. How many engineers does the first one receive?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. One part = 132/(4 + 7) = 12, so the first allocation is 4 parts = 48 engineers.

questions.questionText: y varies inversely as x. If x increases by 10%, what happens to y?
questions.explanationText: Since xy is constant, y is multiplied by 100/110 when x becomes 110% of its value. The new y is 90.91% of the old one, a decrease of 9.09%.

questions.questionText: An amount of Rs. 3300 is divided among Xavier, Yash and Zoya in the ratio 4 : 5 : 2. How much does Yash receive?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The ratio has 4 + 5 + 2 = 11 parts, so one part = 3300/11 = 300. Yash receives 5 parts = Rs. 1500.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 9 and their difference is 35. What is the smaller number?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let the numbers be 4k and 9k. Their difference is 9k - 4k = 5k = 35, so k = 7. The smaller number is 4 x 7 = 28.

questions.questionText: In a survey 35% of the respondents preferred brand X and the rest preferred brand Y. What is the ratio of brand X supporters to brand Y supporters?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If 35% prefer X then 65% prefer Y, so the required ratio is 35 : 65 = 7 : 13.

questions.questionText: Two quantities are 48 and 84. What number must be added to the first quantity so that the ratio of the first to the second becomes 2 : 3?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let x be added. Then (48 + x)/84 = 2/3, so 48 + x = 84 x 2/3 = 56 and x = 8.

questions.questionText: Rs. 1035 is to be shared between two charities in the ratio 2 : 7. What is the smaller share?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Sum of the parts = 2 + 7 = 9, so one part = 1035/9 = Rs. 115. The smaller share is 2 parts = Rs. 230.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 5 : 3, then A is what percentage of B?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Here A is compared with B, not with the total. A/B = 5/3, so A is 5/3 x 100 = 166.67% of B.

questions.questionText: y varies inversely as x. If x increases by 50%, what happens to y?
questions.explanationText: Since xy is constant, y is multiplied by 100/150 when x becomes 150% of its value. The new y is 66.67% of the old one, a decrease of 33.33%.

questions.questionText: Find the third proportional to 4 and 12.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If a : b = b : x then b^2 = ax, so x = b^2/a = 144/4 = 36.

questions.questionText: If 15 identical components cost Rs. 525, how many such components can be bought for Rs. 1050?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The unit rate is 525/15 = Rs. 35 per component. With Rs. 1050 one can buy 1050/35 = 30 components.

questions.questionText: y varies inversely as x. Which of the following statements is true?

options.text: The sum x + y stays constant

questions.explanationText: Inverse variation means y = k/x, that is xy = k, so the product of the two variables is constant while their ratio is not.

questions.questionText: z varies jointly as x and y. When x = 2 and y = 3, z = 24. Find z when x = 4 and y = 5.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Joint variation gives z = kxy with k = 24/(2 x 3) = 4. Therefore z = 4 x 4 x 5 = 80.

questions.questionText: The ratio of a person's income to expenditure is 4 : 3. If the monthly income is Rs. 24000, what are the monthly savings?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Expenditure = income x 3/4 = 24000 x 3/4 = Rs. 18000, so savings = 24000 - 18000 = Rs. 6000.

questions.questionText: Find the ratio of 2 days to 18 hours.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Convert both quantities to the same unit first: 2 days = 48 hours. The required ratio is 48 : 18 = 8 : 3.

questions.questionText: If 4 : 7 = x : 56, what is the value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Cross multiplying 4/7 = x/56 gives 7 x = 4 x 56 = 224, so x = 32.

questions.questionText: The salaries of A and B are in the ratio 7 : 8. If A's salary is increased by 30% and B's salary is decreased by 20%, what is the new ratio of their salaries?
questions.explanationText: Apply each change separately: A becomes 7 x 130/100 = 9.1 and B becomes 8 x 80/100 = 6.4. The new ratio is 9.1 : 6.4 = 91 : 64.

questions.questionText: An amount of Rs. 4000 is divided among four departments in the ratio 2 : 5 : 6 : 7. How much does the department with the largest share receive?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The ratio has 2 + 5 + 6 + 7 = 20 parts, so one part = 4000/20 = 200. The largest share is 7 parts = Rs. 1400.

questions.questionText: Three quantities are in the ratio 4 : 5 : 6. What fraction of the total is the second quantity?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The total has 4 + 5 + 6 = 15 parts and the second quantity is 5 parts, so its fraction of the total is 5/15 = 1/3.

questions.questionText: Divide 990 rupees between two persons in the ratio 4 : 7. What is the larger share?
questions.explanationText: Total number of parts = 4 + 7 = 11, so one part = 990/11 = 90. The larger share corresponds to 7 parts, i.e. 7 x 90 = 630.

questions.questionText: Three partners invest Rs. 4000 for 12 months, Rs. 6000 for 8 months and Rs. 5000 for 6 months. In what ratio should the profit be shared?
questions.explanationText: The profit share is proportional to capital x time: 4000 x 12 = 48000, 6000 x 8 = 48000 and 5000 x 6 = 30000. Simplifying 48000 : 48000 : 30000 gives 8 : 8 : 5.

questions.questionText: The ratio of a person's income to expenditure is 5 : 3. If the monthly income is Rs. 20000, what are the monthly savings?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Expenditure = income x 3/5 = 20000 x 3/5 = Rs. 12000, so savings = 20000 - 12000 = Rs. 8000.

questions.questionText: If 3 : 5 = x : 40, what is the value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Cross multiplying 3/5 = x/40 gives 5 x = 3 x 40 = 120, so x = 24.

questions.questionText: 12 workers can finish a fixed task in 15 days. Working at the same rate, how long will 18 workers take to finish the same task?
questions.explanationText: The number of workers and the time are inversely proportional, so their product is constant: 12 x 15 = 180. With 18 workers the time = 180/18 = 10 days.

questions.questionText: Three amounts are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. What percentage of the total is made up by the first and third amounts together?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. First and third together make 2 + 5 = 7 parts out of 10, so the percentage is 7/10 x 100 = 70%.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 5 and their sum is 64. Find the larger number.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let the numbers be 3k and 5k. Then 3k + 5k = 8k = 64, so k = 8, and the larger number is 5 x 8 = 40.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 5 : 7, then A is what percentage of B?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Here A is compared with B, not with the total. A/B = 5/7, so A is 5/7 x 100 = 71.43% of B.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 3 : 4, and A is multiplied by 2 while B is multiplied by 3, what is the new ratio?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The new values are 3 x 2 = 6 parts and 4 x 3 = 12 parts, so the new ratio is 6 : 12 = 1 : 2.

questions.questionText: Why is it incorrect to write the ratio of 2 m to 50 cm as 2 : 50?

options.text: Because a ratio must always be written in its lowest terms
Because ratios cannot be formed between lengths
Because the larger quantity must always be written second
Because the quantities must be expressed in the same unit first, giving 200 cm : 50 cm = 4 : 1

questions.explanationText: A ratio compares quantities of the same kind measured in the same unit. Converting 2 m to 200 cm gives 200 : 50, which simplifies to 4 : 1.

questions.questionText: Simplify the ratio 4/5 : 6/25.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Divide the two fractions: (4/5) / (6/25) = 10/3. Writing this value as a ratio of whole numbers gives 10 : 3.

questions.questionText: Express 0.35 : 0.49 in the simplest whole-number form.
questions.explanationText: Multiply both terms by a suitable power of 10 to clear the decimals: 0.35 : 0.49 becomes 35 : 49, and dividing by their HCF gives 5 : 7.

questions.questionText: A : B = 5 : 7 and B : C = 3 : 4. If A = 150, what is the value of C?
questions.explanationText: Aligning the common term B gives A : B : C = 15 : 21 : 28. Since A corresponds to 15 parts and A = 150, one part = 10. Hence C = 28 parts = 280.

questions.questionText: Three amounts are in the ratio 2 : 5 : 7. What percentage of the total is made up by the first and third amounts together?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. First and third together make 2 + 7 = 9 parts out of 14, so the percentage is 9/14 x 100 = 64.29%.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 3 : 8, what is (B - A) : A?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Take A = 3k and B = 8k. Then B - A = 5k, so (B - A) : A = 5 : 3 = 5 : 3.

questions.questionText: Arrange the ratios 7 : 10, 2 : 3 and 5 : 7 in ascending order.
questions.explanationText: Convert each ratio to a decimal value: 7 : 10 = 0.7000, 2 : 3 = 0.6667 and 5 : 7 = 0.7143. Arranging these values in increasing order gives 2 : 3, 7 : 10, 5 : 7.

questions.questionText: 4 machines working 9 hours a day produce 288 units. At the same rate, how many units will 10 machines produce in 9 hours?
questions.explanationText: Output varies jointly with the number of machines and the hours worked. The output per machine-hour is 288/(4 x 9) = 8, so 10 machines in 9 hours produce 8 x 10 x 9 = 720 units.

questions.questionText: If A is 7/9 of B, what is A : B?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. A = (7/9) B means A/B = 7/9, so A : B = 7 : 9. The fraction and the ratio carry exactly the same information.

questions.questionText: In a group the ratio of men to women is 4 : 1. What percentage of the group are men?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Men form 4 parts out of a total of 4 + 1 = 5 parts, so the required percentage is 4/5 x 100 = 80%.

questions.questionText: What is the sub-duplicate ratio of 4 : 49?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The sub-duplicate ratio of a : b is the square root of each term: sqrt(4) : sqrt(49) = 2 : 7.

questions.questionText: Four quantities are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 and their total is 2000. What is the difference between the largest and the smallest quantity?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. One part = 2000/10 = 200. The largest is 4 parts and the smallest is 1 parts, so the difference is (4 - 1) x 200 = 600.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 5 : 7, what is (B - A) : A?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Take A = 5k and B = 7k. Then B - A = 2k, so (B - A) : A = 2 : 5 = 2 : 5.

questions.questionText: y varies as the square of x. If x1 : x2 = 2 : 3, what is y1 : y2?
questions.explanationText: Since y is proportional to the square of x, the ratio y1 : y2 equals the square of each term of x1 : x2 = 2 : 3, which gives 4 : 9.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 7 : 10, what is (A + B) : (B - A)?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. With A = 7k and B = 10k, A + B = 17k and B - A = 3k, so the required ratio is 17 : 3 = 17 : 3.

questions.questionText: Find the ratio of 1.5 m to 25 cm.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Convert both quantities to the same unit first: 1.5 m = 150 cm. The required ratio is 150 : 25 = 6 : 1.

questions.questionText: Two ratios a : b and c : d are given with a : b = c : d. Which relation must hold?
questions.explanationText: A proportion a/b = c/d can be cross multiplied to give ad = bc. This is the standard test for four quantities being in proportion.

questions.questionText: Arrange the ratios 2 : 3, 3 : 5 and 5 : 8 in ascending order.
questions.explanationText: Convert each ratio to a decimal value: 2 : 3 = 0.6667, 3 : 5 = 0.6000 and 5 : 8 = 0.6250. Arranging these values in increasing order gives 3 : 5, 5 : 8, 2 : 3.

questions.questionText: Two positive numbers are in the ratio 5 : 6 and their product is 1080. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.explanationText: Let the numbers be 5k and 6k. Their product is 30k^2 = 1080, so k^2 = 36 and k = 6. The numbers are 30 and 36, and their sum is 66.

questions.questionText: y varies inversely as x. If x increases by 25%, what happens to y?
questions.explanationText: Since xy is constant, y is multiplied by 100/125 when x becomes 125% of its value. The new y is 80% of the old one, a decrease of 20%.

questions.questionText: Two positive numbers are in the ratio 4 : 5 and their product is 500. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.explanationText: Let the numbers be 4k and 5k. Their product is 20k^2 = 500, so k^2 = 25 and k = 5. The numbers are 20 and 25, and their sum is 45.

questions.questionText: y varies as the square of x. When x = 4, y = 32. Find y when x = 6.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. y = k x^2 with k = 32/4^2 = 2. Hence when x = 6, y = 2 x 36 = 72.

questions.questionText: A mixture of 48 litres contains petrol and kerosene in the ratio 5 : 3. How many litres of kerosene does it contain?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The mixture has 5 + 3 = 8 parts, so one part = 48/8 = 6 litres. The quantity of kerosene is 3 parts = 18 litres.

questions.questionText: What is the mean proportional between 8 and 18?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If x is the mean proportional between a and b then x^2 = ab = 8 x 18 = 144, so x = 12 for positive quantities.

questions.questionText: Two quantities are 36 and 60. What number must be added to the first quantity so that the ratio of the first to the second becomes 2 : 3?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let x be added. Then (36 + x)/60 = 2/3, so 36 + x = 60 x 2/3 = 40 and x = 4.

questions.questionText: Three friends have Rs. 60, Rs. 120 and Rs. 180, which are in the ratio 1 : 2 : 3. The first gives Rs. 15 to the second, and then the second gives Rs. 25 to the third. What is the final ratio of their amounts?
questions.explanationText: After the first transfer the amounts are 45, 135 and 180. After the second transfer they are 45, 110 and 205, which simplifies to 9 : 22 : 41.

questions.questionText: A mixture of 60 litres contains sand and cement in the ratio 7 : 5. How many litres of cement does it contain?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The mixture has 7 + 5 = 12 parts, so one part = 60/12 = 5 litres. The quantity of cement is 5 parts = 25 litres.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 7. When 2 is subtracted from each of them, the ratio becomes 2 : 5. Find the larger number.
questions.explanationText: Let the numbers be 4k and 7k. Then (4k - 2)/(7k - 2) = 2/5. Cross multiplying gives 5(4k - 2) = 2(7k - 2), from which k = 1. The numbers are 4 and 7, so the larger is 7.

questions.questionText: A quantity is divided between two people in the ratio 7 : 3. What fraction of the whole does the smaller share represent?
questions.explanationText: The total has 7 + 3 = 10 parts and the smaller share is 3 parts, so it is 3/10 of the whole. The fraction 3/7 would be the ratio of the smaller share to the larger share.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 5 : 6 and B : C = 9 : 11, what is A : B : C?
questions.explanationText: Make the B terms equal. Multiply A : B = 5 : 6 by 9 to get 45 : 54, and B : C = 9 : 11 by 6 to get 54 : 66. Hence A : B : C = 15 : 18 : 22.

questions.questionText: The ratio of a person's income to expenditure is 7 : 5. If the monthly income is Rs. 28000, what are the monthly savings?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Expenditure = income x 5/7 = 28000 x 5/7 = Rs. 20000, so savings = 28000 - 20000 = Rs. 8000.

questions.questionText: If 6 : 11 = x : 77, what is the value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Cross multiplying 6/11 = x/77 gives 11 x = 6 x 77 = 462, so x = 42.

questions.questionText: y varies as the cube of x. If x1 : x2 = 3 : 4, what is y1 : y2?
questions.explanationText: Since y is proportional to the cube of x, the ratio y1 : y2 equals the cube of each term of x1 : x2 = 3 : 4, which gives 27 : 64.

questions.questionText: The efficiencies of two workers A and B are in the ratio 3 : 5. If they work separately on the same job, what is the ratio of the times they take?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed amount of work, time is inversely proportional to efficiency. Hence the ratio of times is the inverse of the efficiency ratio, 5 : 3.

questions.questionText: Two trains cover the same distance. If the ratio of their speeds is 3 : 4, what is the ratio of the times they take?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed, so the ratio of times is the inverse of the speed ratio: 4 : 3.

questions.questionText: Rs. 2080 is to be shared between two vendors in the ratio 3 : 10. What is the smaller share?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Sum of the parts = 3 + 10 = 13, so one part = 2080/13 = Rs. 160. The smaller share is 3 parts = Rs. 480.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 8 : 9, and A is multiplied by 2 while B is multiplied by 5, what is the new ratio?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The new values are 8 x 2 = 16 parts and 9 x 5 = 45 parts, so the new ratio is 16 : 45 = 16 : 45.

questions.questionText: 12 machines working 5 hours a day produce 900 units. At the same rate, how many units will 7 machines produce in 5 hours?
questions.explanationText: Output varies jointly with the number of machines and the hours worked. The output per machine-hour is 900/(12 x 5) = 15, so 7 machines in 5 hours produce 15 x 7 x 5 = 525 units.

questions.questionText: y varies as the square of x. When x = 2, y = 50. Find y when x = 5.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. y = k x^2 with k = 50/2^2 = 12.5. Hence when x = 5, y = 12.5 x 25 = 312.5.

questions.questionText: Two quantities are 24 and 108. What number must be added to the first quantity so that the ratio of the first to the second becomes 1 : 3?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let x be added. Then (24 + x)/108 = 1/3, so 24 + x = 108 x 1/3 = 36 and x = 12.

questions.questionText: A mixture of 54 litres contains acid and water in the ratio 2 : 7. How many litres of water does it contain?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The mixture has 2 + 7 = 9 parts, so one part = 54/9 = 6 litres. The quantity of water is 7 parts = 42 litres.

questions.questionText: The fourth proportional to 10, 35 and 16 is required for a scale drawing. What is its value?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. For a : b = c : x, cross multiplication gives x = bc/a = (35 x 16)/10 = 56.

questions.questionText: y varies directly as x. If x increases by 20%, by what percentage does y change?
questions.explanationText: Direct variation means y = kx, so multiplying x by 120/100 multiplies y by the same factor. Hence y also increases by 20%.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 4 : 7 and the difference between their ages is 15 years. What is the age of the older person?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let the ages be 4k and 7k years. The difference is 3k = 15, so k = 5. The older person is 7 x 5 = 35 years old.

questions.questionText: What is the compound ratio of 7 : 10 and 5 : 14?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The compound ratio of a : b and c : d is ac : bd. Here it is (7 x 5) : (10 x 14) = 35 : 140 = 1 : 4.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 2 : 11 and their sum is 91. Find the larger number.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let the numbers be 2k and 11k. Then 2k + 11k = 13k = 91, so k = 7, and the larger number is 11 x 7 = 77.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 7 : 9 and the difference between their ages is 10 years. What is the age of the older person?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let the ages be 7k and 9k years. The difference is 2k = 10, so k = 5. The older person is 9 x 5 = 45 years old.

questions.questionText: If x : y = 3 : 7, what is the ratio 1/x : 1/y?
questions.explanationText: 1/x : 1/y = (1/3k) : (1/7k) = 7 : 3 after multiplying both terms by 21k, so the reciprocal ratio is the inverse ratio 7 : 3.

questions.questionText: Find the ratio of 2 m to 50 cm.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Convert both quantities to the same unit first: 2 m = 200 cm. The required ratio is 200 : 50 = 4 : 1.

questions.questionText: If A is 5/8 of B, what is A : B?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. A = (5/8) B means A/B = 5/8, so A : B = 5 : 8. The fraction and the ratio carry exactly the same information.

questions.questionText: Two square plots have areas 6 sq m and 24 sq m. What is the mean proportional between these two areas?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The mean proportional x satisfies x^2 = 6 x 24 = 144, so x = 12.

questions.questionText: Three friends have Rs. 180, Rs. 240 and Rs. 300, which are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. The first gives Rs. 30 to the second, and then the second gives Rs. 20 to the third. What is the final ratio of their amounts?
questions.explanationText: After the first transfer the amounts are 150, 270 and 300. After the second transfer they are 150, 250 and 320, which simplifies to 15 : 25 : 32.

questions.questionText: z varies directly as x^2 and inversely as y. If x1 : x2 = 3 : 5 and y1 : y2 = 2 : 7, what is z1 : z2?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. z1/z2 = (x1/x2)^2 x (y2/y1) = (3/5)^2 x (7/2) = 63/50, so z1 : z2 = 63 : 50.

questions.questionText: The fourth proportional to 15, 25 and 21 is required for a scale drawing. What is its value?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. For a : b = c : x, cross multiplication gives x = bc/a = (25 x 21)/15 = 35.

questions.questionText: Divide 1620 rupees between two persons in the ratio 5 : 4. What is the larger share?
questions.explanationText: Total number of parts = 5 + 4 = 9, so one part = 1620/9 = 180. The larger share corresponds to 5 parts, i.e. 5 x 180 = 900.

questions.questionText: Find the fourth proportional to 9, 15 and 24.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If a : b = c : x then ax = bc, so x = bc/a = (15 x 24)/9 = 40.

questions.questionText: Two quantities are 60 and 96. What number must be added to the first quantity so that the ratio of the first to the second becomes 3 : 4?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let x be added. Then (60 + x)/96 = 3/4, so 60 + x = 96 x 3/4 = 72 and x = 12.

questions.questionText: A total of 180 items is split in the ratio 4 : 5. By how much does the larger group exceed the smaller group?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. One part = 180/9 = 20 items. The difference is 1 parts = 20 items.

questions.questionText: The salaries of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 4. If A's salary is increased by 10% and B's salary is decreased by 25%, what is the new ratio of their salaries?
questions.explanationText: Apply each change separately: A becomes 3 x 110/100 = 3.3 and B becomes 4 x 75/100 = 3. The new ratio is 3.3 : 3 = 11 : 10.

questions.questionText: Which of the following ratios is greater: 4 : 9 or 5 : 12?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Compare by cross multiplication: 4 x 12 = 48 and 5 x 9 = 45. Since 48 > 45, the ratio 4 : 9 is greater.

questions.questionText: Two quantities are in the ratio 7 : 10. If 30% of the first quantity is removed and the second is unchanged, what is the new ratio?
questions.explanationText: Removing 30% leaves 70% of the first quantity: 7 x 70/100 = 4.9 parts. The second remains 10 parts, so the new ratio is 4.9 : 10 = 49 : 100.

questions.questionText: Express 1.25 : 2.5 in the simplest whole-number form.
questions.explanationText: Multiply both terms by a suitable power of 10 to clear the decimals: 1.25 : 2.5 becomes 125 : 250, and dividing by their HCF gives 1 : 2.

questions.questionText: The salaries of A and B are in the ratio 5 : 7. If A's salary is decreased by 20% and B's salary is increased by 40%, what is the new ratio of their salaries?
questions.explanationText: Apply each change separately: A becomes 5 x 80/100 = 4 and B becomes 7 x 140/100 = 9.8. The new ratio is 4 : 9.8 = 20 : 49.

questions.questionText: Divide 1200 rupees between two persons in the ratio 5 : 7. What is the larger share?
questions.explanationText: Total number of parts = 5 + 7 = 12, so one part = 1200/12 = 100. The larger share corresponds to 7 parts, i.e. 7 x 100 = 700.

questions.questionText: Simplify the ratio 1/2 : 3/10.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Divide the two fractions: (1/2) / (3/10) = 5/3. Writing this value as a ratio of whole numbers gives 5 : 3.

questions.questionText: Divide 364 books between two persons in the ratio 6 : 7. What is the larger share?
questions.explanationText: Total number of parts = 6 + 7 = 13, so one part = 364/13 = 28. The larger share corresponds to 7 parts, i.e. 7 x 28 = 196.

questions.questionText: A and B have amounts in the ratio 3 : 5. If B gives Rs. 10 to A, their amounts become in the ratio 5 : 7. How much did A have originally?
questions.explanationText: Let the amounts be Rs. 3k and Rs. 5k. After the transfer, (3k + 10)/(5k - 10) = 5/7. Cross multiplying and simplifying gives k = 30, so A originally had Rs. 90 and B had Rs. 150 (check: 100 and 140 are in the ratio 5 : 7).

questions.questionText: Find the ratio of 3 km to 750 m.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Convert both quantities to the same unit first: 3 km = 3000 m. The required ratio is 3000 : 750 = 4 : 1.

questions.questionText: In a group the ratio of men to women is 5 : 3. What percentage of the group are men?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Men form 5 parts out of a total of 5 + 3 = 8 parts, so the required percentage is 5/8 x 100 = 62.50%.

questions.questionText: What is the compound ratio of 4 : 9 and 3 : 2?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The compound ratio of a : b and c : d is ac : bd. Here it is (4 x 3) : (9 x 2) = 12 : 18 = 2 : 3.

questions.questionText: z varies directly as the square of x and inversely as y. When x = 3 and y = 9, z = 12. What is z when x = 6 and y = 4?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. z = k x^2 / y, so k = z y / x^2 = 12 x 9 / 9 = 12. Then z = 12 x 6^2 / 4 = 108.

questions.questionText: If 5 : 8 = x : 72, what is the value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Cross multiplying 5/8 = x/72 gives 8 x = 5 x 72 = 360, so x = 45.

questions.questionText: If a : b = 5 : 6, find the value of (1a + 1b) : (2a + 3b).
questions.explanationText: Take a = 5k and b = 6k. Then the first expression = 1(5k) + 1(6k) = 11k and the second = 28k, so the required ratio is 11 : 28 = 11 : 28.

questions.questionText: If 8, x and 18 are in continued proportion, what is the positive value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. In a continued proportion a : x = x : c, so x^2 = ac = 8 x 18 = 144 and x = 12.

questions.questionText: An amount of Rs. 1540 is divided among Priya, Qadir and Rahul in the ratio 3 : 4 : 7. How much does Qadir receive?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The ratio has 3 + 4 + 7 = 14 parts, so one part = 1540/14 = 110. Qadir receives 4 parts = Rs. 440.

questions.questionText: Rs. 1872 is to be shared between two contractors in the ratio 7 : 9. What is the smaller share?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Sum of the parts = 7 + 9 = 16, so one part = 1872/16 = Rs. 117. The smaller share is 7 parts = Rs. 819.

questions.questionText: A total of 200 items is split in the ratio 3 : 7. By how much does the larger group exceed the smaller group?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. One part = 200/10 = 20 items. The difference is 4 parts = 80 items.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 9 : 13. When 6 is subtracted from each of them, the ratio becomes 3 : 5. Find the larger number.
questions.explanationText: Let the numbers be 9k and 13k. Then (9k - 6)/(13k - 6) = 3/5. Cross multiplying gives 5(9k - 6) = 3(13k - 6), from which k = 2. The numbers are 18 and 26, so the larger is 26.

questions.questionText: If a : b = 3 : 4, find the value of (2a + 1b) : (1a + 2b).
questions.explanationText: Take a = 3k and b = 4k. Then the first expression = 2(3k) + 1(4k) = 10k and the second = 11k, so the required ratio is 10 : 11 = 10 : 11.

questions.questionText: What is the mean proportional between 3 and 27?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If x is the mean proportional between a and b then x^2 = ab = 3 x 27 = 81, so x = 9 for positive quantities.

questions.questionText: y varies directly as x. If x increases by 30%, by what percentage does y change?
questions.explanationText: Direct variation means y = kx, so multiplying x by 130/100 multiplies y by the same factor. Hence y also increases by 30%.

questions.questionText: Three quantities are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 4. What fraction of the total is the second quantity?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The total has 1 + 3 + 4 = 8 parts and the second quantity is 3 parts, so its fraction of the total is 3/8 = 3/8.

questions.questionText: Which of the following ratios is greater: 2 : 3 or 5 : 8?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Compare by cross multiplication: 2 x 8 = 16 and 5 x 3 = 15. Since 16 > 15, the ratio 2 : 3 is greater.

questions.questionText: The present ages of two persons are in the ratio 2 : 3. After 4 years their ages will be in the ratio 5 : 7. What is the present age of the younger person?
questions.explanationText: Let the ages be 2k and 3k. After 4 years, (2k + 4)/(3k + 4) = 5/7. Cross multiplying gives k = 8, so the ages are 16 and 24 years; the younger is 16 years old.

questions.questionText: Find the third proportional to 5 and 15.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If a : b = b : x then b^2 = ax, so x = b^2/a = 225/5 = 45.

questions.questionText: The salaries of A and B are in the ratio 4 : 5. If A's salary is increased by 25% and B's salary is increased by 10%, what is the new ratio of their salaries?
questions.explanationText: Apply each change separately: A becomes 4 x 125/100 = 5 and B becomes 5 x 110/100 = 5.5. The new ratio is 5 : 5.5 = 10 : 11.

questions.questionText: The salaries of A and B are in the ratio 2 : 3. If A's salary is increased by 50% and B's salary is increased by 20%, what is the new ratio of their salaries?
questions.explanationText: Apply each change separately: A becomes 2 x 150/100 = 3 and B becomes 3 x 120/100 = 3.6. The new ratio is 3 : 3.6 = 5 : 6.

questions.questionText: If (x + 6) : (x - 5) = 11 : 8, what is the value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Cross multiplying, 8(x + 6) = 11(x - 5), so 8x + 48 = 11x - 55. Collecting terms gives 3x = 103 and x = 34.33.

questions.questionText: What is the sub-duplicate ratio of 9 : 16?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The sub-duplicate ratio of a : b is the square root of each term: sqrt(9) : sqrt(16) = 3 : 4.

questions.questionText: Two trains cover the same distance. If the ratio of their speeds is 7 : 8, what is the ratio of the times they take?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed, so the ratio of times is the inverse of the speed ratio: 8 : 7.

questions.questionText: Find the ratio of 2 hours to 45 minutes.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Convert both quantities to the same unit first: 2 hours = 120 minutes. The required ratio is 120 : 45 = 8 : 3.

questions.questionText: If 18 identical components cost Rs. 756, how many such components can be bought for Rs. 2800?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The unit rate is 756/18 = Rs. 42 per component. With Rs. 2800 one can buy 2800/42 = 66.67 components.

questions.questionText: Find the fourth proportional to 3, 8 and 12.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If a : b = c : x then ax = bc, so x = bc/a = (8 x 12)/3 = 32.

questions.questionText: If 5 notebooks cost Rs. 150, what will 12 notebooks cost at the same rate?
questions.explanationText: The cost varies directly with the quantity, so cost/quantity is constant: 150/5 = 30 per unit. Therefore 12 units cost 30 x 12 = Rs. 360.

questions.questionText: In a survey 25% of the respondents preferred brand X and the rest preferred brand Y. What is the ratio of brand X supporters to brand Y supporters?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If 25% prefer X then 75% prefer Y, so the required ratio is 25 : 75 = 1 : 3.

questions.questionText: Two trains cover the same distance. If the ratio of their speeds is 5 : 6, what is the ratio of the times they take?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed, so the ratio of times is the inverse of the speed ratio: 6 : 5.

questions.questionText: Three partners invest Rs. 8000 for 6 months, Rs. 6000 for 12 months and Rs. 9000 for 4 months. In what ratio should the profit be shared?
questions.explanationText: The profit share is proportional to capital x time: 8000 x 6 = 48000, 6000 x 12 = 72000 and 9000 x 4 = 36000. Simplifying 48000 : 72000 : 36000 gives 4 : 6 : 3.

questions.questionText: Find the ratio of 6 rupees to 150 paise.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Convert both quantities to the same unit first: 6 rupees = 600 paise. The required ratio is 600 : 150 = 4 : 1.

questions.questionText: Two square plots have areas 5 sq m and 80 sq m. What is the mean proportional between these two areas?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The mean proportional x satisfies x^2 = 5 x 80 = 400, so x = 20.

questions.questionText: Are the ratios 6 : 9 and 10 : 15 equivalent?
questions.explanationText: Reduce each ratio to its simplest form: 6 : 9 = 2 : 3 and 10 : 15 = 2 : 3. Alternatively compare the cross products 6 x 15 = 90 and 9 x 10 = 90. The ratios are therefore equal.

questions.questionText: Two positive numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3 and their product is 294. What is the sum of the two numbers?
questions.explanationText: Let the numbers be 2k and 3k. Their product is 6k^2 = 294, so k^2 = 49 and k = 7. The numbers are 14 and 21, and their sum is 35.

questions.questionText: A : B = 3 : 4 and B : C = 2 : 7. If A = 90, what is the value of C?
questions.explanationText: Aligning the common term B gives A : B : C = 3 : 4 : 14. Since A corresponds to 6 parts and A = 90, one part = 15. Hence C = 28 parts = 420.

questions.questionText: Two trains cover the same distance. If the ratio of their speeds is 2 : 9, what is the ratio of the times they take?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed distance, time is inversely proportional to speed, so the ratio of times is the inverse of the speed ratio: 9 : 2.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 2 : 5 and B : C = 3 : 7, what is A : B : C?
questions.explanationText: Make the B terms equal. Multiply A : B = 2 : 5 by 3 to get 6 : 15, and B : C = 3 : 7 by 5 to get 15 : 35. Hence A : B : C = 6 : 15 : 35.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 8 and their difference is 45. What is the smaller number?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let the numbers be 3k and 8k. Their difference is 8k - 3k = 5k = 45, so k = 9. The smaller number is 3 x 9 = 27.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 7 : 9 and B : C = 3 : 5, what is A : B : C?
questions.explanationText: Make the B terms equal. Multiply A : B = 7 : 9 by 3 to get 21 : 27, and B : C = 3 : 5 by 9 to get 27 : 45. Hence A : B : C = 7 : 9 : 15.

questions.questionText: Three quantities are in the ratio 2 : 5 : 7. What fraction of the total is the second quantity?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The total has 2 + 5 + 7 = 14 parts and the second quantity is 5 parts, so its fraction of the total is 5/14 = 5/14.

questions.questionText: Three friends have Rs. 60, Rs. 90 and Rs. 150, which are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 5. The first gives Rs. 20 to the second, and then the second gives Rs. 10 to the third. What is the final ratio of their amounts?
questions.explanationText: After the first transfer the amounts are 40, 110 and 150. After the second transfer they are 40, 100 and 160, which simplifies to 2 : 5 : 8.

questions.questionText: z varies jointly as x and y. When x = 4 and y = 6, z = 48. Find z when x = 2 and y = 9.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Joint variation gives z = kxy with k = 48/(4 x 6) = 2. Therefore z = 2 x 2 x 9 = 36.

questions.questionText: Four quantities are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5 : 6 and their total is 3600. What is the difference between the largest and the smallest quantity?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. One part = 3600/18 = 200. The largest is 6 parts and the smallest is 3 parts, so the difference is (6 - 3) x 200 = 600.

questions.questionText: The fourth proportional to 8, 20 and 14 is required for a scale drawing. What is its value?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. For a : b = c : x, cross multiplication gives x = bc/a = (20 x 14)/8 = 35.

questions.questionText: y varies inversely as x. When x = 4, y = 15. Find y when x = 6.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Inverse variation means xy = k, so k = 4 x 15 = 60. When x = 6, y = 60/6 = 10.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 3 : 8 and B : C = 4 : 9, what is A : B : C?
questions.explanationText: Make the B terms equal. Multiply A : B = 3 : 8 by 4 to get 12 : 32, and B : C = 4 : 9 by 8 to get 32 : 72. Hence A : B : C = 3 : 8 : 18.

questions.questionText: If 16, x and 25 are in continued proportion, what is the positive value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. In a continued proportion a : x = x : c, so x^2 = ac = 16 x 25 = 400 and x = 20.

questions.questionText: 6 printers can finish a fixed task in 40 minutes. Working at the same rate, how long will 15 printers take to finish the same task?
questions.explanationText: The number of printers and the time are inversely proportional, so their product is constant: 6 x 40 = 240. With 15 printers the time = 240/15 = 16 minutes.

questions.questionText: Express 0.75 : 1.5 in the simplest whole-number form.
questions.explanationText: Multiply both terms by a suitable power of 10 to clear the decimals: 0.75 : 1.5 becomes 75 : 150, and dividing by their HCF gives 1 : 2.

questions.questionText: Simplify the ratio 7/8 : 21/32.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Divide the two fractions: (7/8) / (21/32) = 4/3. Writing this value as a ratio of whole numbers gives 4 : 3.

questions.questionText: z varies directly as the square of x and inversely as y. When x = 2 and y = 4, z = 10. What is z when x = 3 and y = 5?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. z = k x^2 / y, so k = z y / x^2 = 10 x 4 / 4 = 10. Then z = 10 x 3^2 / 5 = 18.

questions.questionText: Two square plots have areas 3 sq m and 48 sq m. What is the mean proportional between these two areas?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The mean proportional x satisfies x^2 = 3 x 48 = 144, so x = 12.

questions.questionText: 171 crates are to be allocated to two warehouses in the ratio 5 : 4. How many crates does the first one receive?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. One part = 171/(5 + 4) = 19, so the first allocation is 5 parts = 95 crates.

questions.questionText: If (x + 2) : (x - 3) = 5 : 3, what is the value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Cross multiplying, 3(x + 2) = 5(x - 3), so 3x + 6 = 5x - 15. Collecting terms gives 2x = 21 and x = 10.5.

questions.questionText: The salaries of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 5. If A's salary is increased by 20% and B's salary is decreased by 10%, what is the new ratio of their salaries?
questions.explanationText: Apply each change separately: A becomes 3 x 120/100 = 3.6 and B becomes 5 x 90/100 = 4.5. The new ratio is 3.6 : 4.5 = 4 : 5.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 4 : 9, what is (A + B) : (B - A)?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. With A = 4k and B = 9k, A + B = 13k and B - A = 5k, so the required ratio is 13 : 5 = 13 : 5.

questions.questionText: Rs. 1425 is to be shared between two suppliers in the ratio 8 : 11. What is the smaller share?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Sum of the parts = 8 + 11 = 19, so one part = 1425/19 = Rs. 75. The smaller share is 8 parts = Rs. 600.

questions.questionText: If (x + 4) : (x - 1) = 7 : 5, what is the value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Cross multiplying, 5(x + 4) = 7(x - 1), so 5x + 20 = 7x - 7. Collecting terms gives 2x = 27 and x = 13.5.

questions.questionText: If 25, x and 36 are in continued proportion, what is the positive value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. In a continued proportion a : x = x : c, so x^2 = ac = 25 x 36 = 900 and x = 30.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 2 : 3, then A is what percentage of B?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Here A is compared with B, not with the total. A/B = 2/3, so A is 2/3 x 100 = 66.67% of B.

questions.questionText: If 9, x and 16 are in continued proportion, what is the positive value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. In a continued proportion a : x = x : c, so x^2 = ac = 9 x 16 = 144 and x = 12.

questions.questionText: The ratio of two numbers is 2 : 3. If 8 is added to the first number, the ratio becomes 3 : 4. What is the second number?
questions.explanationText: Let the numbers be 2k and 3k. Then (2k + 8)/(3k) = 3/4. Cross multiplying, 4(2k + 8) = 3 x 3k, which gives k = 32. Hence the numbers are 64 and 96, and the second is 96.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 6 : 13 and their difference is 56. What is the smaller number?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let the numbers be 6k and 13k. Their difference is 13k - 6k = 7k = 56, so k = 8. The smaller number is 6 x 8 = 48.

questions.questionText: The number of men and women in an office is in the ratio 3 : 7. If 4 more men and 4 more women join, the ratio becomes 1 : 2. How many men were there originally?
questions.explanationText: Let the numbers be 3k and 7k. Then (3k + 4)/(7k + 4) = 1/2. Cross multiplying gives k = 4, so there were 12 men and 28 women originally (check: 16 : 32 = 1 : 2).

questions.questionText: Are the ratios 15 : 25 and 21 : 35 equivalent?
questions.explanationText: Reduce each ratio to its simplest form: 15 : 25 = 3 : 5 and 21 : 35 = 3 : 5. Alternatively compare the cross products 15 x 35 = 525 and 25 x 21 = 525. The ratios are therefore equal.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 2 : 7, B : C = 3 : 4 and C : D = 5 : 2, find A : D.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. A/D = (A/B) x (B/C) x (C/D) = (2/7) x (3/4) x (5/2) = 30/56, so A : D = 15 : 28.

questions.questionText: In a survey 12% of the respondents preferred brand X and the rest preferred brand Y. What is the ratio of brand X supporters to brand Y supporters?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If 12% prefer X then 88% prefer Y, so the required ratio is 12 : 88 = 3 : 22.

questions.questionText: Are the ratios 8 : 12 and 14 : 20 equivalent?
questions.explanationText: Reduce each ratio to its simplest form: 8 : 12 = 2 : 3 and 14 : 20 = 7 : 10. Alternatively compare the cross products 8 x 20 = 160 and 12 x 14 = 168. The ratios are therefore not equal.

questions.questionText: If x : y = 5 : 8, what is the ratio 1/x : 1/y?
questions.explanationText: 1/x : 1/y = (1/5k) : (1/8k) = 8 : 5 after multiplying both terms by 40k, so the reciprocal ratio is the inverse ratio 8 : 5.

questions.questionText: Three amounts are in the ratio 4 : 5 : 6. What percentage of the total is made up by the first and third amounts together?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. First and third together make 4 + 6 = 10 parts out of 15, so the percentage is 10/15 x 100 = 66.67%.

questions.questionText: In a group the ratio of men to women is 5 : 7. What percentage of the group are men?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Men form 5 parts out of a total of 5 + 7 = 12 parts, so the required percentage is 5/12 x 100 = 41.67%.

questions.questionText: In a group the ratio of men to women is 2 : 3. What percentage of the group are men?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Men form 2 parts out of a total of 2 + 3 = 5 parts, so the required percentage is 2/5 x 100 = 40%.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 3 : 5, B : C = 2 : 3 and C : D = 4 : 7, find A : D.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. A/D = (A/B) x (B/C) x (C/D) = (3/5) x (2/3) x (4/7) = 24/105, so A : D = 8 : 35.

questions.questionText: The population of a town is 64000 and the ratio of adults to children is 9 : 7. How many children are there?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. One part = 64000/(9 + 7) = 4000. The number of children is 7 parts = 28000.

questions.questionText: The efficiencies of two workers A and B are in the ratio 2 : 7. If they work separately on the same job, what is the ratio of the times they take?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed amount of work, time is inversely proportional to efficiency. Hence the ratio of times is the inverse of the efficiency ratio, 7 : 2.

questions.questionText: y varies as the square of x. When x = 3, y = 108. Find y when x = 4.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. y = k x^2 with k = 108/3^2 = 12. Hence when x = 4, y = 12 x 16 = 192.

questions.questionText: If 7 identical motors cost Rs. 2100, what will 11 identical motors cost at the same rate?
questions.explanationText: The cost varies directly with the quantity, so cost/quantity is constant: 2100/7 = 300 per unit. Therefore 11 units cost 300 x 11 = Rs. 3300.

questions.questionText: What is the sub-duplicate ratio of 25 : 36?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The sub-duplicate ratio of a : b is the square root of each term: sqrt(25) : sqrt(36) = 5 : 6.

questions.questionText: Divide 560 chocolates between two persons in the ratio 2 : 5. What is the larger share?
questions.explanationText: Total number of parts = 2 + 5 = 7, so one part = 560/7 = 80. The larger share corresponds to 5 parts, i.e. 5 x 80 = 400.

questions.questionText: Find the fourth proportional to 4, 6 and 10.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If a : b = c : x then ax = bc, so x = bc/a = (6 x 10)/4 = 15.

questions.questionText: Two quantities are in the ratio 5 : 7. If 20% of the first quantity is removed and the second is unchanged, what is the new ratio?
questions.explanationText: Removing 20% leaves 80% of the first quantity: 5 x 80/100 = 4 parts. The second remains 7 parts, so the new ratio is 4 : 7 = 4 : 7.

questions.questionText: An amount of Rs. 1800 is divided among Priya, Qadir and Rahul in the ratio 2 : 3 : 7. How much does Qadir receive?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The ratio has 2 + 3 + 7 = 12 parts, so one part = 1800/12 = 150. Qadir receives 3 parts = Rs. 450.

questions.questionText: If A is 3/4 of B, what is A : B?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. A = (3/4) B means A/B = 3/4, so A : B = 3 : 4. The fraction and the ratio carry exactly the same information.

questions.questionText: In a group the ratio of men to women is 7 : 3. What percentage of the group are men?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Men form 7 parts out of a total of 7 + 3 = 10 parts, so the required percentage is 7/10 x 100 = 70%.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 2 : 3 and B : C = 4 : 5, what is A : B : C?
questions.explanationText: Make the B terms equal. Multiply A : B = 2 : 3 by 4 to get 8 : 12, and B : C = 4 : 5 by 3 to get 12 : 15. Hence A : B : C = 8 : 12 : 15.

questions.questionText: 8 machines can finish a fixed task in 21 hours. Working at the same rate, how long will 14 machines take to finish the same task?
questions.explanationText: The number of machines and the time are inversely proportional, so their product is constant: 8 x 21 = 168. With 14 machines the time = 168/14 = 12 hours.

questions.questionText: The population of a town is 45000 and the ratio of males to females is 5 : 4. How many females are there?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. One part = 45000/(5 + 4) = 5000. The number of females is 4 parts = 20000.

questions.questionText: The number of men and women in an office is in the ratio 5 : 9. If 8 more men and 8 more women join, the ratio becomes 3 : 5. How many men were there originally?
questions.explanationText: Let the numbers be 5k and 9k. Then (5k + 8)/(9k + 8) = 3/5. Cross multiplying gives k = 8, so there were 40 men and 72 women originally (check: 48 : 80 = 3 : 5).

questions.questionText: y varies inversely as x. When x = 3, y = 40. Find y when x = 15.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Inverse variation means xy = k, so k = 3 x 40 = 120. When x = 15, y = 120/15 = 8.

questions.questionText: A and B have amounts in the ratio 7 : 9. If B gives Rs. 8 to A, their amounts become in the ratio 9 : 11. How much did A have originally?
questions.explanationText: Let the amounts be Rs. 7k and Rs. 9k. After the transfer, (7k + 8)/(9k - 8) = 9/11. Cross multiplying and simplifying gives k = 40, so A originally had Rs. 280 and B had Rs. 360 (check: 288 and 352 are in the ratio 9 : 11).

questions.questionText: Two square plots have areas 7 sq m and 63 sq m. What is the mean proportional between these two areas?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The mean proportional x satisfies x^2 = 7 x 63 = 441, so x = 21.

questions.questionText: A mixture of 25 litres contains milk and water in the ratio 3 : 2. How many litres of water does it contain?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The mixture has 3 + 2 = 5 parts, so one part = 25/5 = 5 litres. The quantity of water is 2 parts = 10 litres.

questions.questionText: Divide 450 tickets between two persons in the ratio 7 : 8. What is the larger share?
questions.explanationText: Total number of parts = 7 + 8 = 15, so one part = 450/15 = 30. The larger share corresponds to 8 parts, i.e. 8 x 30 = 240.

questions.questionText: If z varies jointly as x and y, and both x and y are doubled, what happens to z?

options.text: z becomes four times its original value
z becomes eight times its original value

questions.explanationText: Joint variation gives z = kxy. Replacing x by 2x and y by 2y gives k(2x)(2y) = 4kxy, so z becomes four times the original value.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 2 : 3, B : C = 4 : 5 and C : D = 6 : 7, find A : D.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. A/D = (A/B) x (B/C) x (C/D) = (2/3) x (4/5) x (6/7) = 48/105, so A : D = 16 : 35.

questions.questionText: If 6 kg of steel cost Rs. 450, what will 15 kg of steel cost at the same rate?
questions.explanationText: The cost varies directly with the quantity, so cost/quantity is constant: 450/6 = 75 per unit. Therefore 15 units cost 75 x 15 = Rs. 1125.

questions.questionText: Three quantities are in the ratio 3 : 4 : 5. What fraction of the total is the second quantity?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The total has 3 + 4 + 5 = 12 parts and the second quantity is 4 parts, so its fraction of the total is 4/12 = 1/3.

questions.questionText: Four quantities are in the ratio 2 : 3 : 4 : 5 and their total is 2800. What is the difference between the largest and the smallest quantity?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. One part = 2800/14 = 200. The largest is 5 parts and the smallest is 2 parts, so the difference is (5 - 2) x 200 = 600.

questions.questionText: In class A there are 50 students with boys and girls in the ratio 3 : 7, and in class B there are 30 students with boys and girls in the ratio 1 : 2. If the two classes are combined, what is the ratio of boys to girls?
questions.explanationText: Class A has 50 x 3/10 = 15 boys and class B has 30 x 1/3 = 10 boys, giving 25 boys in all. The remaining 55 students are girls, so the combined ratio is 5 : 11.

questions.questionText: If A : B = 4 : 9, what is (B - A) : A?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Take A = 4k and B = 9k. Then B - A = 5k, so (B - A) : A = 5 : 4 = 5 : 4.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 4 : 7 and their sum is 143. Find the larger number.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let the numbers be 4k and 7k. Then 4k + 7k = 11k = 143, so k = 13, and the larger number is 7 x 13 = 91.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 7 : 9. When 4 is subtracted from each of them, the ratio becomes 3 : 4. Find the larger number.
questions.explanationText: Let the numbers be 7k and 9k. Then (7k - 4)/(9k - 4) = 3/4. Cross multiplying gives 4(7k - 4) = 3(9k - 4), from which k = 4. The numbers are 28 and 36, so the larger is 36.

questions.questionText: Two square plots have areas 2 sq m and 8 sq m. What is the mean proportional between these two areas?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The mean proportional x satisfies x^2 = 2 x 8 = 16, so x = 4.

questions.questionText: What is the mean proportional between 12 and 27?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If x is the mean proportional between a and b then x^2 = ab = 12 x 27 = 324, so x = 18 for positive quantities.

questions.questionText: If A is 2/5 of B, what is A : B?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. A = (2/5) B means A/B = 2/5, so A : B = 2 : 5. The fraction and the ratio carry exactly the same information.

questions.questionText: The efficiencies of two workers A and B are in the ratio 5 : 6. If they work separately on the same job, what is the ratio of the times they take?
questions.explanationText: For a fixed amount of work, time is inversely proportional to efficiency. Hence the ratio of times is the inverse of the efficiency ratio, 6 : 5.

questions.questionText: In class A there are 40 students with boys and girls in the ratio 3 : 2, and in class B there are 35 students with boys and girls in the ratio 4 : 3. If the two classes are combined, what is the ratio of boys to girls?
questions.explanationText: Class A has 40 x 3/5 = 24 boys and class B has 35 x 4/7 = 20 boys, giving 44 boys in all. The remaining 31 students are girls, so the combined ratio is 44 : 31.

questions.questionText: A and B have amounts in the ratio 5 : 7. If B gives Rs. 12 to A, their amounts become in the ratio 7 : 9. How much did A have originally?
questions.explanationText: Let the amounts be Rs. 5k and Rs. 7k. After the transfer, (5k + 12)/(7k - 12) = 7/9. Cross multiplying and simplifying gives k = 48, so A originally had Rs. 240 and B had Rs. 336 (check: 252 and 324 are in the ratio 7 : 9).

questions.questionText: A : B = 4 : 9 and B : C = 5 : 2. If A = 100, what is the value of C?
questions.explanationText: Aligning the common term B gives A : B : C = 20 : 45 : 18. Since A corresponds to 20 parts and A = 100, one part = 5. Hence C = 18 parts = 90.

questions.questionText: Find the fourth proportional to 5, 12 and 15.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If a : b = c : x then ax = bc, so x = bc/a = (12 x 15)/5 = 36.

questions.questionText: y varies inversely as x. If x increases by 20%, what happens to y?
questions.explanationText: Since xy is constant, y is multiplied by 100/120 when x becomes 120% of its value. The new y is 83.33% of the old one, a decrease of 16.67%.

questions.questionText: Find the third proportional to 8 and 20.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If a : b = b : x then b^2 = ax, so x = b^2/a = 400/8 = 50.

questions.questionText: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 9 and their sum is 112. Find the larger number.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Let the numbers be 5k and 9k. Then 5k + 9k = 14k = 112, so k = 8, and the larger number is 9 x 8 = 72.

questions.questionText: z varies directly as the square root of x and inversely as y. When x = 4 and y = 3, z = 16. Find z when x = 9 and y = 2.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. z = k sqrt(x) / y, so k = z y / sqrt(x) = 16 x 3 / 2 = 24. Then z = 24 x 3 / 2 = 36.

questions.questionText: A and B have amounts in the ratio 2 : 5. If B gives Rs. 15 to A, their amounts become in the ratio 3 : 4. How much did A have originally?
questions.explanationText: Let the amounts be Rs. 2k and Rs. 5k. After the transfer, (2k + 15)/(5k - 15) = 3/4. Cross multiplying and simplifying gives k = 15, so A originally had Rs. 30 and B had Rs. 75 (check: 45 and 60 are in the ratio 3 : 4).

questions.questionText: z varies directly as the square of x and inversely as y. When x = 4 and y = 2, z = 20. What is z when x = 2 and y = 5?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. z = k x^2 / y, so k = z y / x^2 = 20 x 2 / 16 = 2.5. Then z = 2.5 x 2^2 / 5 = 2.

questions.questionText: Which of the following ratios is greater: 5 : 8 or 7 : 11?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Compare by cross multiplication: 5 x 11 = 55 and 7 x 8 = 56. Since 55 < 56, the ratio 7 : 11 is greater.

questions.questionText: If 8 metres of cable cost Rs. 600, what will 14 metres of cable cost at the same rate?
questions.explanationText: The cost varies directly with the quantity, so cost/quantity is constant: 600/8 = 75 per unit. Therefore 14 units cost 75 x 14 = Rs. 1050.

questions.questionText: If 4, x and 9 are in continued proportion, what is the positive value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. In a continued proportion a : x = x : c, so x^2 = ac = 4 x 9 = 36 and x = 6.

questions.questionText: z varies jointly as x and y. When x = 5 and y = 2, z = 40. Find z when x = 3 and y = 7.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Joint variation gives z = kxy with k = 40/(5 x 2) = 4. Therefore z = 4 x 3 x 7 = 84.

questions.questionText: y varies directly as x. When x = 3, y = 12. What is the value of y when x = 7?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Direct variation means y = kx with k = y/x = 12/3 = 4. Hence when x = 7, y = 4 x 7 = 28.

questions.questionText: If 7 : 3 = x : 27, what is the value of x?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Cross multiplying 7/3 = x/27 gives 3 x = 7 x 27 = 189, so x = 63.

questions.questionText: What is the compound ratio of 5 : 6 and 8 : 15?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. The compound ratio of a : b and c : d is ac : bd. Here it is (5 x 8) : (6 x 15) = 40 : 90 = 4 : 9.

questions.questionText: Find the third proportional to 9 and 15.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If a : b = b : x then b^2 = ax, so x = b^2/a = 225/9 = 25.

questions.questionText: Simplify the ratio 5/6 : 10/9.
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. Divide the two fractions: (5/6) / (10/9) = 3/4. Writing this value as a ratio of whole numbers gives 3 : 4.

questions.questionText: 10 workers can finish a fixed task in 36 days. Working at the same rate, how long will 24 workers take to finish the same task?
questions.explanationText: The number of workers and the time are inversely proportional, so their product is constant: 10 x 36 = 360. With 24 workers the time = 360/24 = 15 days.

questions.questionText: What is the mean proportional between 4 and 9?
questions.explanationText: Set up the ratio as a pair of parts of a common unit, keep the quantities in the same unit, and use the proportion or variation relation that the situation requires. If x is the mean proportional between a and b then x^2 = ab = 4 x 9 = 36, so x = 6 for positive quantities.

questions.questionText: Divide 720 rupees between two persons in the ratio 3 : 5. What is the larger share?
questions.explanationText: Total number of parts = 3 + 5 = 8, so one part = 720/8 = 90. The larger share corresponds to 5 parts, i.e. 5 x 90 = 450.
